newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says it not involved in killing Austrians.
newsitem.headline: Israel says it not involved in killing Austrians.

text.p: The Israeli army said two Austrian U.N. soldiers killed on the Golan Heights on Friday were shot eight km (five miles) from Israeli lines and Israeli troops were not involved in the incident.
"We are talking about a position eight kilometres inside Syria and it cannot be that Israeli soldiers shot at them," an army spokeswoman said.
The Austrian Defence Ministry said in Vienna that two Austrian soldiers serving with a United Nations force were shot dead during a foot patrol on the Golan Heights between Syria and Israel.
The ministry said one of the men was a junior officer and the other a soldier, but it did not name them or give any details of the circumstances of their deaths. It said an inquiry was under way.
An Israeli security source said the incident occurred in an area in which smugglers between Syria and Lebanon are active.

The U.N. Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) serves as a buffer between the Syrian and Israeli armies on the Golan Heights. The 1,050-member force has been deployed since 1974 to monitor a ceasefire and troop withdrawal that followed the 1973 Middle East war. Austria has more than 400 soldiers stationed on the Golan Heights.
